findings.title: Attachments hardcoded as [] — audio/video/image never checked for duplicates
findings.description: The PR title explicitly claims it adds duplicate-checking support for audio, video, and image attachments. However, in the new analyze.py the `run_duplicate_check` call always passes `[]` as the attachments list, discarding the actual `attachments` variable that was passed into `_process_analyze_job`. The old code passed `attachments or []`, meaning real attachment payloads were forwarded to the similarity engine. The new code never forwards them, so the media-type checking described in the PR title is never exercised — this is a functional regression for attachment-based duplicate detection.
findings.recommendation: Pass the actual `attachments` variable (or its normalized equivalent `normalized_attachments`) instead of `[]`. If attachment-based checking is intentionally deferred, the PR title and description must be corrected and a follow-up ticket filed.

findings.title: run_duplicate_check called with None query when workflow produces no final_answer
findings.description: When `final_answer` is `None` (workflow failure or no answer), `build_duplicate_check_query` returns `None`, and `run_duplicate_check(None, [], ...)` is still called unconditionally. The behavior of `check_duplicate_analysis(None, [])` is not modified in this PR and is undefined from the diff context. This may error, return a misleading 'no duplicate' result, or trigger unexpected retry logic.
findings.recommendation: Guard the duplicate-check call: if `build_duplicate_check_query(final_answer)` returns `None`, skip the call and set `duplicate_check_data` to a 'skipped' sentinel.

findings.title: Ordering change: LLM workflow always runs even for known duplicates — wasted compute
findings.description: Previously, duplicate checking ran before the workflow as an early-exit gate. Now the workflow always runs first and the duplicate check follows, meaning all LLM/workflow compute is incurred even when the submission is a known duplicate. The retry_attempt counter is consumed by the workflow before the duplicate check can short-circuit. This is a semantic regression in cost and throughput for the duplicate-submission path.
findings.recommendation: Clarify whether the goal is post-hoc deduplication only. If early-exit is desired for cost savings, keep a pre-workflow check and add a post-workflow title-based check. If post-hoc only, explicitly document the trade-off.

findings.title: build_duplicate_check_query returns None for whitespace-only/prefix-only titles with no observable signal
findings.description: If `final_answer.title` is empty or becomes empty after prefix stripping (e.g. a title that is only a classification prefix like 'FALSO:'), `normalized_title` is falsy and the function returns `None`. This silently skips the duplicate check with no log, metric, or error. The caller in `analyze.py` does not distinguish this case from `final_answer is None`.
findings.recommendation: Log or emit a metric when a non-None `final_answer` produces a `None` query, so pathological titles that bypass duplicate checking are observable in production.

findings.title: None-query downstream path not tested in integration
findings.description: Tests verify `build_duplicate_check_query` in isolation but do not test what happens when the returned `None` is passed to `run_duplicate_check`. If `check_duplicate_analysis(None, [])` raises or returns an incorrect result, no test will catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add an integration-level or mock-based test in `test_similarity_worker.py` verifying behavior when `final_answer` is `None`.
